software.name: influence-index-bibliometrics
software.title: Influence Index: a log-based measure of research influence for institutions (MATLAB, processed data)

article.citation: C. Voyant, J. Baas, R. Boverhof, P. Stringari, M. Marchand-Lasserre, J. P. A. Ioannidis. A log-based influence index for evaluating research institutions
article.status: manuscript in submission: title and principle only, no result reported here

supported: compute the Influence Index of an institution from public Top 2 % data

inputs.definition: highly cited authors of the institution
processed data from the Stanford–Elsevier Top 2 % lists

outputs.definition: change between the current and the historical index

rules: Never invent a value. Each input is given by the user, an exact unit conversion of a given value, or a documented default that the user explicitly accepts.
Use the canonical unit of each field; convert exactly and say so (for example 2 km -> 2000 m). Never mix a percentage and a fraction.
Ask when a request is ambiguous or a required input is missing; do not infer a number from a place name or a qualitative word.
Run the code unmodified. Report only what was actually computed, with quantity, unit and the input values used; never present a planned or unavailable run as a result.
State the scope and the limits below when you report a result.
Citation-based indicators are proxies, not judgments of individuals or of quality.
limits: Manuscript in submission: report the formula and the code, not institutional results.
